what: The sleep-cycle token, handed round the roster by the cairn device. token.py: roster() (alpha-sorted device ids whose probes/ folder holds sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py, read from the ground loop's own disk roster every call), mint() (open a cycle, hand the token to roster[0]; an empty roster closes at once as 'nothing to visit'; an open cycle is superseded and kept), receive_answer() (a device's answer: refused loudly when stale or out of turn, else recorded under visited and the next hand or the close), standing() (the standing cycle from instance-space). The cairn device fronts it with two verbs — sleep-token (a device's answer) and sleep-cycle (mint | show) — in cairn/devices/cairn/device.py.
why: One token rotation replaces N independent sleep daemons — the same move the ground loop made for heartbeats — and it is serial by design (measured OOM history n=3; which sleep cycles are independent is unknown). The shape is a HUB because Probe.to is static and a probe may not import the roster: cairn hands to one device at a time and every device answers cairn, which hands onward. The announce feed is the RECORD of the rotation (n+1 records per complete cycle), never its transport — the bus delivers only on personal.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.sleep_cycle import token`; `token.mint(bus, roots=None, roster_root=None)`; `token.receive_answer(bus, body, roots=None)`; `token.standing(roots=None)`; `token.roster(root=None)`. Over the bus: verb `sleep-cycle` to cairn with body {"act": "mint"|"show"}; verb `sleep-token` is what a device's probe pokes (cairn/tools/base/mail_probe.py makes that three lines).
entry: FRESH design under ticket bf146e9e3967 (child of 4de7baf7e255 sleep-cycle-token), decisions D1–D7 on the ticket; composes bus.post, BaseShim's beat and poke, _FeedbackDevice's mailbox and discovery.device_folders — nothing grafted.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter once a voyage freezes here (Law 5). Runtime state is instance-space only: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/sleep_cycle/cycle.json (the standing cycle) and superseded.jsonl (open cycles a later mint replaced).
filed_edges: (a) no live device carries sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py yet — 'what sleep work is' is out of this ticket's bounds (constrain-20260906T105321-ac8cedd9d817), so the live roster is empty and a live mint closes as 'nothing to visit'; the parent's WATCHME(sleep-rotation-completes) watches the live rotation.
(b) the idle trigger that mints a cycle is ticket 9b6b392ebcfe; today a mint is the sleep-cycle verb with act mint.
(c) a device that never answers holds the token forever; nothing here times a hand out — a stalled cycle is visible (standing() shows an open cycle with position < len(roster)) but not yet loud.
gates: proof gate (tester) — proofs/test_token_rotation.py on BusDevice.scratch: order, single holder, n+1 announce records, close once, stale id refused, empty roster closes; durability gate — git commit.
falsifier: RED on any of: a token that stops at a device that answered; two devices holding an unanswered token at once; a complete rotation over n devices leaving other than n+1 announce records for its cycle_id; a stale or out-of-turn answer accepted; a cycle closing twice or never; an empty roster that does not close at mint.
how_it_learns: It does not. The rotation is a mechanism; what is learned from the answers each device returns is the parent ticket's question (4de7baf7e255), read off the announce feed and cycle.json.
